records.name: Proteomics & phosphoproteomics (es)
records.text: Medir las proteínas de un tumor, que es lo que realmente atacan los fármacos, en vez de los genes que las codifican.

records.name: Proteomics & phosphoproteomics (de)

records.name: Imaging mass cytometry (simple)
records.text: Imaging mass cytometry stains a tumour slice for dozens of proteins at once using metal-tagged antibodies read by a mass spectrometer, mapping which cells are where.

records.name: Proteomics & phosphoproteomics (simple)
records.text: Measuring the proteins in a tumour, which is what drugs actually hit.

effective.effectiveText: This approach measures several protein markers in a tissue section, in one or more imaging cycles. Image analysis then estimates cells, counts and distances under defined rules.
A way to stain a tumour slice for dozens of proteins at once using metal-tagged antibodies read by a mass spectrometer, giving a detailed map of which cells are where.
Medir las proteínas de un tumor, que es lo que realmente atacan los fármacos, en vez de los genes que las codifican.
RPPA spots tiny amounts of protein extract from many tumours onto a slide and probes them with antibodies, measuring a few hundred proteins and phosphoproteins in each sample at once.
These methods measure RNA signals while keeping information about position in a tissue section. A measured spot, an estimated cell boundary and an imputed value are different kinds of evidence.
Mass-spectrometry proteomics identifies protein-derived peptides and can quantify signals under a defined workflow. It does not measure every protein or directly establish a cell's activity.

This array tests protein extracts from many samples using selected antibodies. The panel and its validation determine which protein signals can be interpreted.
A targeted protein assay measures selected peptide signals through a defined workflow. Reliable amounts require evidence about the quantitative range and precision of the assay.
Image analysis estimates which pixels or detected molecules belong to each cell. Those assignments affect the measurements reported for that cell.
A test may detect that a signal is present before it can measure its amount reliably. Both limits need to be defined for the method and sample conditions.
